lines.japanese: あ、どーもどーも初めましてコンニチワ～。元気？　平和？　青春？
lines.english: “Oh, hi there, hi there. Pleased to meet you. Hellooo. How are you? Healthy? Peaceful? Youthful?”

lines.japanese: はいはい、俺は元気ですよ平和ですよ青春ですよ？
lines.english: “Uh-huh, uh-huh. Me, I'm healthy, peaceful, and youthful. Thanks for asking.”

lines.japanese: でー、今日はいったい、どういったご用件でこちらへ？
lines.english: “Sooo, what exactly brings you here today?”

lines.japanese: ──なんてね。
lines.english: “—Just kidding.”

lines.japanese: あれでしょ、お迎えさんでしょ？　帰ってこいって？　グレタガルド？
lines.english: “I know what this is. You've come to fetch me, right? Tell me it's time to go back? To Gretagard?”

lines.japanese: あー、そっすよねー、もうかなり安定してますもんねー。えぇえぇ、そろそろだと思ってましたよー。
lines.english: “Ahh, right, right. Things have been pretty stable for a while now. Mm-hm, mm-hm. I knew it must be about time.”

lines.japanese: んー、でも？　あれ？　まだ、ちょーっとだけ時期尚早じゃないすか？
lines.english: “Mm, but? Wait. Isn't it still just a teensy bit early?”

lines.japanese: ああ、来たる日まで監視ってこと？　やだなあ、べつに逃げやしませんよ。
lines.english: “Oh, so you're here to keep an eye on me until the big day? Come on, I'm not going anywhere.”

lines.japanese: ──他のふたりが逃げないならね。
lines.english: “—As long as the other two don't, that is.”

lines.japanese: そうそう。ところで、アナタのお名前とか伺っちゃってもよろしいですか？　や、だって、ねえ？　これからしばらくのお付き合いになるわけだし？　自己紹介ぐらい、ねえ？
lines.english: Right, right. So, um, would it perhaps be all right if I asked your name? I mean, you know? We're gonna be together for a while, right? So we could at least introduce ourselves, right?

lines.japanese: あ、俺っすか？
lines.english: “Oh, me?”

lines.japanese: 俺は千歳鷲介、しがない貧乏フリーターっす。社会の底辺でちょこちょこヌルいバイトしながら、ま、適当に生きながらえてきました、ええ。
lines.english: I'm Shusuke Chitose, a poor little perennial part-timer. Been scraping by at the bottom of society, doing one easy little odd job after another. Yeah, just kind of surviving.

lines.japanese: たとえばほら……あるでしょ、登録制の派遣会社とか。働きたい日の前日なんかに電話して、仕事があればもらうって感じの。そーゆーの、いくつか登録したりしてまして。
lines.english: “You know the kind of place—a temp agency where you register, call the day before you feel like working, and take a job if they've got one. I'm signed up with a few of those.”

lines.japanese: え、具体的にですか？　んー、そっすねー、最近やった仕事ってーと……。
lines.english: “You want specifics? Hmm, let's see. Jobs I've done lately...”

lines.japanese: ま、イベント会場の設営・撤収は定番として、それから交通量調査、ポスティング、ティッシュ配り、ダイレクトメールのラベル貼り、シューズの箱詰め。あと遊園地の着ぐるみなんかも。それプラス在宅仕事が少々。
lines.english: “Setting up and tearing down event venues is the old standby. Then there’s traffic counting, delivering flyers, handing out promotional tissues, sticking labels on direct mail, packing shoes into boxes. I’ve even worn a mascot suit at an amusement park. Plus a little work I do from home.”

lines.japanese: や、飽きっぽいわけじゃないんですけどねー。分かるでしょ、ひとところに落ちつくのが出来ないタチですから。
lines.english: “No, it isn't that I get bored easily. You understand, don't you? I'm just not built to settle down in one place.”

lines.japanese: 千歳鷲介・さすらいの自由人──なんてね。どうすかコレ。良くないすかコレ？
lines.english: “Shusuke Chitose, wandering free spirit—just kidding. How's that? Pretty good, right?”

lines.japanese: まあ、でも？　負け惜しみかもしんないけど？　毎回いろんな場所でいろんなひとに出会えるってのは、それだけでわりと楽しいもんでしたよ。
lines.english: “Then again, maybe that's just sour grapes. Still, there was something pretty fun about meeting all kinds of people in a different place every time.”

lines.japanese: ええ。俺は誰かさんと違って、ひととお話するのとか、それはもう大好きですから。
lines.english: Yep. Unlike somebody I could name, I just looove talking to people.

lines.japanese: ま、聞いてる方が楽っちゃ楽っすけどね。でも自分が話さなきゃ、相手だっておいそれとは口開いてくれないでしょ。
lines.english: I mean, yeah, listening is easier. But if you don't talk, the other person isn't gonna just open up, right?

lines.japanese: とと！　だからってこう、だらだら自分のことばっかり話しちゃうってのは最悪っすよね。ええ、すいません。で、アナタは何してるひと？
lines.english: “Whoops! That said, droning on and on about yourself is the absolute worst, isn't it? Yes, sorry about that. So, what do you do?”

lines.japanese: ……あら、ずいぶんと寡黙なんすねえ。アレすか。男は黙って、てやつすか。うゎお、かーっくいー！　ほーんと、死神みたーい。
lines.english: “...Well, you’re awfully quiet. What is it, that old ‘real men keep their mouths shut’ line? Wooow, so cooool! Just like the Grim Reaper.”

lines.japanese: てか死神っすもんねえ、ぶっちゃけ。ねえ、そんなよーなもんでしょ実際。なあ、そうなんだろ。
lines.english: “Though honestly, you are the Grim Reaper. More or less, right? That's what you are, isn't it? Come on. Tell me I'm right.”

lines.japanese: はあ……。
lines.english: “Haaah...”

lines.japanese: ま、いいや。アナタが何者だろうと、どーせ俺の事態は変わらないんだろうし。せいぜい残りの人生を……残りの人生？　あらら、いやな言葉だねえ。
lines.english: “Oh, well. Whoever you are, I suppose my situation won't change. I'll just make the most of the life I have left... The life I have left? Yikes. That's an ugly phrase.”

lines.japanese: ま、でも人間なんて、例外なく皆さんいつかは土に還っちゃうわけですから？　ええ、言いかえれば、オギャアと生まれて以来ずっと、残りの日を指折り数えているわけですよね。
lines.english: “Then again, every human being returns to the earth one day, without exception. Put another way, from the moment we come bawling into the world, we're already counting down the days we have left.”

lines.japanese: だったら、ねえ？　楽しみましょうよ、残りの人生を。せっかくなんだから。
lines.english: “So why not enjoy it? The rest of our lives, I mean. Since we're here.”

lines.japanese: 俺はそうしますよ。気ままに面白おかしく堪能させていただきますよ。
lines.english: “I know I will. I'll savor mine however I please and have a grand old time doing it.”

lines.japanese: ええ、たとえば今夜。うん、みんなで楽しく騒いじゃうの。土曜の夜だしね、もアゲアゲでね。がっつりアゲアゲでね。ふふん、いいでしょ？
lines.english: “Take tonight, for example. Yeah, we'll all get together and make some noise. It's Saturday night, so we'll get crazy hyped. Totally, ridiculously hyped. Heh heh. Sounds good, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: アナタもね、そんなむっつり黙ってないで、たまにはこう、大声出したりして人生楽しんだ方がいいっすよ？　人間っていうのはね、楽しむために生まれてきたんです。
lines.english: “And you—quit sitting there all tight-lipped. You ought to shout your head off once in a while and enjoy life, you know? Human beings were born to have fun.”

lines.japanese: ──なんてね。これ、むかし近所にいた立派なおじいさんに教わった言葉なんすけどね。しかも、かなり歪曲した解釈なんすけどね。あ、原文知りたい？
lines.english: —just kidding. It's something this fine old guy from my neighborhood taught me a long time ago. Though I'm twisting it pretty badly. Oh, wanna hear the original?

lines.japanese: しーん……。
lines.english: “Deeead silence...”

lines.japanese: て、リアクションなしかよオイィィィ！
lines.english: “Hey! Seriously? Nothing? Not even a reaction?!”

lines.japanese: や、素晴らしい。さすがですね、アナタ。相手を頭から否定することなく、海のような広い心で受けとめるその包容力。オトナですねー。１００の言葉より１の沈黙ってわけですか。かっくいー！
lines.english: “No, wonderful. Truly wonderful. That's you all over. You never reject a fellow out of hand; you take him in with a heart as broad as the sea. Such maturity. One silence worth a hundred words—is that it? So cooool!”

lines.japanese: 俺には無理っすね、そーゆーの。なんかしか喋ってないと落ちつかなくて。えぇえぇ、まだモンゴルヒップの子供っすから。口先だけで生きてますから。寂しいと死んじゃうウサギさんっすから。
lines.english: “I couldn’t pull that off. I get restless when I’m not talking. Mm-hm, mm-hm. Still a baby, blue birthmark on my ass and all. My mouth’s all I’ve got. I’m a little bunny who’d die of loneliness.”

lines.japanese: しぃーん……。
lines.english: “Deeeead silence...”

lines.japanese: ハイ！　またもやリアクションなし！　っと。
lines.english: “Yep! Still no reaction! Aaaand moving on.”

lines.japanese: あの……俺、話つづけていいすか？　いい？　そうですか？
lines.english: “So... can I keep talking? I can? Well, all right, then.”

lines.japanese: じゃお言葉に甘えて──えーと、ああほら、柳木原にグローヴ通りっていうおしゃれロードがあるじゃないですか。ほら、あの、アルバトロスの横入ってったとこ。グローヴ街とも言うんですけどね。
lines.english: “Then don't mind if I do—let's see. Oh, you know Grove Street in Yanagihara, that fashionable little strip? The one you turn into beside the Albatross. They call the neighborhood the Grove too.”

lines.japanese: 知らないカナー……ま、いいや。あのね、あるところにアレキサンダーって名前のレストランがあるんですよ。
lines.english: “Maybe you don't know it... Oh, well. Anyway, there's a restaurant there called Alexander.”

lines.japanese: ほら俺、自炊とかしないひとじゃないすか。だからよくそこに、ごはん食べに行くんすよ。
lines.english: “Come on, you know I never cook for myself. So I go there to eat pretty often.”

lines.japanese: でー、これは昨日の話なんですけどね──
lines.english: “And this happened yesterday—”

lines.japanese: ああ、いやいや、これは失礼いたしました。どぞどぞ、長くなりますんで、ええ、楽にしてください楽に。あー、コーヒーか紅茶でもお出ししましょうか？
lines.english: “Oh—no, no. How rude of me. This will take a while, so please, please, make yourself comfortable. Shall I bring you coffee or tea?”

lines.japanese: はは！　ないっすけどね、ここにはそんな気の利いたもん。
lines.english: “Ha! Not that we have anything that fancy around here.”
